A.explanation: Too small by factor 100. It results from using radius in $\text{cm}$ without converting to $\text{m}$ and using only one force.

B.explanation: This is half the required value. It treats the separation as $8.0 \text{ cm}$ but counts only one $F \times r$ moment instead of the sum from both sides.

C.explanation: The two forces form a couple of separation $0.080 \text{ m}$, so $20 = F \times 0.080$ gives $F = 250 \text{ N}$.

D.explanation: This is twice the required value. It uses only one radius $0.040 \text{ m}$ as the separation, giving $F = 20 / 0.040$.

hints: Notice the diagram shows two equal opposite $F$ forces on opposite edges of the $4.0 \text{ cm}$ radius lid, so they form a couple not a single moment.
Recall torque from a couple is $F$ times the perpendicular distance between the two lines of action, which here is the diameter of the lid.
Convert $4.0 \text{ cm}$ to metres to get separation $0.080 \text{ m}$, then set $20 \text{ N m} = F \times 0.080 \text{ m}$ and solve for $F$.
walkthrough: Identify the system: two tangential forces $F$ on opposite sides of a lid of radius $r = 4.0 \text{ cm} = 0.040 \text{ m}$ act in opposite directions.
State the rule: each force gives a moment $F \times r$ about the centre in the same rotational sense, so total torque is $T = Fr + Fr = F \times 2r$.
Find the separation: $2r = 2 \times 0.040 \text{ m} = 0.080 \text{ m}$, which is the perpendicular distance between the forces for the couple formula $T = F \times d$.
Substitute the required torque: $20 \text{ N m} = F \times 0.080 \text{ m}$.
Solve: $F = 20 / 0.080 = 250 \text{ N}$ with unit $\text{N}$, as $\text{N m} / \text{m} = \text{N}$. This is option C.
